claim: Generic a lion is glossed using any lion that exists.
evidence_summary: CGEL’s own generic about Italians and pasta tolerates individual exceptions.
finding: An unrestricted domain does not require that the predicate hold of every member. The book gives generic a restricted technical use.
inference: Does lack of a contextual restriction make a generic true of every individual?

evidence.passage: §8.3, p. 407. Generic a lion is glossed using any lion that exists.
evidence.example: Compare the any-lion gloss with CGEL’s own generalization about Italians and pasta. An Italian who dislikes pasta can belong to the intended population without making the generic unusable.
evidence.establishes: Including every individual in the domain leaves open whether the property must hold of every individual. The chapter’s restricted technical sense of generic matters here.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
